To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Routine use of laxatives in addition to carbohydrate loading and oral nutrition supplements within an enhanced-recovery after surgery programme for patients undergoing liver resection may expedite gastrointestinal and overall recovery”.
routine use of laxatives and ONS in patients undergoing liver resection is not associated with any benefit in terms of postoperative outcomes.

1) the use of a laxative and ONS within an enhanced recovery program after liver resection may not expedite the time to first flatus or tolerance to food; 2) however, it may reduce the time to first bowel movement and may reduce the incidence of post-operative nausea and vomiting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the use of a new type of laxatives, the so-called “stimulant laxatives” in the treatment of chronic constipation.
the study of the effect of the effect of a new ERAS programme with routine laxatives and ONS in patients undergoing liver surgery.
the following questions: What is the role of the gut in the pathogenesis of liver disease?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
routine laxatives are not beneficial in patients undergoing liver resection.
routine laxatives and ONS are safe, and that routine laxatives may expediate recovery of gastrointestinal function.
the use of routine laxatives in the postoperative period following major abdominal surgery is associated with an earlier return of gastrointestinal function and earlier oral intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of a laxative to an enhanced recovery programme following liver resection did not expedite recovery of gastrointestinal function.
the use of routine laxatives and ONS in an ERAS programme for liver resection may expedite the recovery of the gastrointestinal tract, but not overall recovery, and may not be cost-effective.

the combination of ONS and laxatives within an ERAS programme is associated with earlier return of bowel function and a shorter overall hospital stay, without any increase in postoperative complications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a laxative and ONS can be used to expedite gastrointestinal recovery within the context of an ERAS protocol.
the use of routine laxatives in the perioperative period may be associated with a faster return of bowel function after liver resection.
routine laxatives may be used in conjunction with an enhanced recovery after liver surgery (ERAS-Liver) protocol.
